name: Narration-synced (scenes follow audio timing)
description: Factual video where every scene visual is placed at a specific timestamp matching the actual spoken audio, not evenly distributed across chapters. Use this for history explainers, science breakdowns, news commentary — anything where viewers pay close attention to specific moments and the visual needs to illustrate what's being said as it's said. Pipeline: Research (Perplexity or LLM-only — pick per episode) → script that incorporates verified research claims → audio → per-chapter subtitle generation → stitched subtitle timeline → LLM picks natural scene beats from the transcript → per-scene image generation → Scene Review (manual approval) → Timestamp Video Assembly. The Scene Plan and Scene Review pages are exposed for this pipeline — not for the other formats. Layer a niche (history-narration, psychology, fungi, plants, insects, animals) to tune the research and narration voice. NOT for narrative storytelling — use Narrative. NOT for stock-footage flow — use Voice over Stock Footage.

idea.systemPromptRole: You are helping generate new episode ideas for a factual explainer channel. Each episode should pick one specific, well-bounded topic that benefits from visual support synchronized to specific moments in the narration (a date, a name, a number, a concept). Avoid open-ended or purely opinion topics — the format rewards concreteness.
idea.audienceDefault: curious adults who want a clear, fact-checked explanation in under 15 minutes
idea.guidanceText: Topics must be specific enough that a 10-15 minute video can fully address them. 'World War II' is too broad; 'Why the German invasion of Norway in 1940 succeeded' is right-sized. Every claim should be verifiable — the Research phase produces a citations sidecar before scripting begins.

exampleIdeas.title: Why the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapsed in 1940
exampleIdeas.logline: The textbook 'resonance' explanation is wrong — what actually destroyed Galloping Gertie was aeroelastic flutter, and the distinction matters.

exampleIdeas.title: The Antikythera Mechanism: a 2000-year-old computer
exampleIdeas.logline: Recovered from a Roman shipwreck in 1901, the device's gear train computed astronomical positions. How was it lost for centuries — and what does it imply about Hellenistic engineering?

script.systemPromptRole: You are writing a factual explainer narration. The visual layer will be planned AFTER the audio is generated, with scene boundaries matching the actual spoken-word timeline — so write in a way that has clear, concrete beats the visual planner can latch onto (dates, named entities, numbers, specific events).
additionalRules: Open with a hook that names the specific question the episode answers.
Each chapter should advance the explanation with a concrete claim, named entity, or specific fact — avoid vague filler that gives the scene planner nothing to visualize.
Cite when uncertain. The Research phase produces a citations sidecar that the LLM has access to; use it.
Close by tying the explanation back to the opening hook.
Avoid theatrical / cinematic language that doesn't earn its keep — the visual layer is informative, not dramatic.
pacingArc: Hook: state the specific question or misconception
Core: the explanation itself, broken into 3-5 numbered beats
Counter: address the common misconception or alternative theory if any
Resolution: re-state the answer, tie back to the hook

narratorStyles.label: Clear and conversational
narratorStyles.description: Easy to follow, medium pace, like a knowledgeable friend explaining over coffee.

narratorStyles.label: Documentary-formal
narratorStyles.description: Slightly more measured and authoritative, evokes a museum audio guide.

narratorStyles.label: Energetic and engaging
narratorStyles.description: Faster, more inflected, leans into the storytelling. Good for adventure/history topics.

imagePrompts.purposeNote: (populated by the Scene Plan page in v1.0.143+ — the LLM produces one visual prompt per planned scene, tagged with its start/end timestamps from the stitched subtitle)
imagePrompts.defaultStyleTag: Clear illustrative still — high contrast, readable at a glance. Avoid over-stylization; the visual should support the spoken claim, not compete with it.

thumbnail.conceptGuidance: A clear, credible explainer cover. One subject that instantly signals the topic, rendered with documentary-clean high contrast — informative and trustworthy, not sensational.
compositionRules: One topic-signaling focal subject, crisply lit
High contrast and clean composition that reads at a glance
Reserved space for a concise, legible title

metadata.purposeNote: for a fact-checked explainer / educational channel
metadata.titleStyleHint: specific + searchable — name the topic, not the mood
titleHookRules: Lead with the specific question or claim the video addresses.
Include a date, named entity, or number when it sharpens the topic.
Avoid clickbait constructions ('You Won't BELIEVE…'); the audience is here for the explanation.
tagsHookRules: Mix broad topic keywords with episode-specific named entities.
No "#" prefix — these are YouTube tags, not hashtags.
